title: MaxTask
description: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxTask is the permanent record of one piece of work done in a database (research, an import, a review or a proof), never pruned while anything points at it.

task_id.description: This task's own id: a random UUID created once by the writer and never reused.

task_type.description: What kind of work this is; a task of type other permits none of the gated actions of rules R-24, R-28 and R-31.

task_type_as_written.description: The kind of work in the writer's own words, given when task_type is other.

status.description: Where the work stands, changed only through the helper's task command (pending, processing, then done, failed or escalated; on_hold pauses it; a task made by mistake or retracted is cancelled, never deleted).

priority.description: How urgent the task is, from 1 (lowest) to 10 (highest).

kind.description: Which documented payload this is: interview, person_request, person_page_session, fan_survey, run, find_original, import_file, analysis, or (G-04, additive) incoming_finding: one finding from another tree (a relative's file as suggestions, a findings delivery), holding its proposed facts and any proposed new person in the payload (sender_tree_id, sender_label, received_at, verdict, person_id or new_person and relation, facts) until the person lets it in; it is never a claim on the person's people while it waits.

person_id.description: The person this task is about (a fan_survey, a person request or a review of a child's main parents); read through merge redirects.

person_ids.description: The persons this task is about, when it concerns more than one.

record_id.description: On a find_original task: the record (often an index entry) whose original image is to be found and looked at.

target_task_id.description: On a judge_review task: the task being reviewed.

payload.description: The task's input, an open object whose documented kinds are interview, person_request, person_page_session, fan_survey (person_id), run (run_id, on a judge_review task), find_original (record_id), import_file (format: gedcom7, gedcom551, gedcomx, gramps_xml, rootsmagic, maxgen (another MAXGEN database, with source_database_id) or other; file_name) and analysis (an imported write-up, as a child task of its import).

result.description: What the work found and decided, in a closed, readable shape.

provenance.description: Helper-owned and written once: who did the work of this task, filled when the task is first claimed (moved to processing) or created already done.

created_by.description: The agent id of the session that wrote this task: optional in input, filled by the helper from the writing session, required in stored form, and a different value is refused (R-14).

started_at.description: Helper-owned: when the task was first moved to processing.

completed_at.description: Helper-owned: when the task reached done, failed or cancelled.

is_living_flag.description: Living A floor: true when the task names or concerns someone who may be alive (unsure means true); it only rises, and while it is true the task must be first_party_only.

contributor_eligibility.description: Who may be given this task: first_party_only (the person's own kit and agents, the default, failing closed) or any_contributor; it must be first_party_only whenever is_living_flag is true.

assigned_to.description: The agent id now working on this task; absent while it is pending.

cost_usd.description: What the work actually cost, in US dollars.

cost_cap_usd.description: The most this task may cost, in US dollars; the agent stops and escalates before going over it.

retry_count.description: How many times the task has been retried after a failure.

max_retries.description: How many retries are allowed before the task is left failed.

error_message.description: What went wrong, when the task failed or was escalated.

escalation_reason.description: Why the task was escalated for a further decision.

queue_file_path.description: The task's path in a file-based queue on this computer; private, never exported.

depends_on.description: Tasks that must be done before this one can start.

parent_task_id.description: The task that made this task (on MaxTask this replaces created_by_task_id, which tasks may not carry).

acceptance_criteria.description: Plain, checkable conditions that a complete result must meet.

min_confidence.description: The lowest result confidence that can be accepted.

evidence_required.description: What the worker must hand back as proof of the work (addresses, exact queries, records saved).

deadline.description: When the work should be finished.

verdict.description: The outcome of a task or step: key_finding (confirmed or found), usable (a usable lead), inconclusive (mixed), ruled_out (proved this is not the right person or record, a disproof), dead_end (searched and found nothing), inaccessible (could not search because of a login, a prohibition or the site being offline; never filed as dead_end), infra (a support task) or other.

description.description: One line saying what this task was.

hypothesis_tested.description: The claim or link this task tested.

why_this_matters.description: Why the work was done, in terms of the person's goal.

what_we_did_and_result.description: What was done and the headline result, in plain words.

how_results_affect_goal.description: How the result moves the person's goal forward or back.

what_we_did_with_results.description: What was written or changed because of the result.

steps.description: One entry per search or lookup performed; these steps are the only search log (the dead_end view is read from them).

verdict.description: The outcome of the task as a whole.

verdict_as_written.description: The outcome in the writer's own words, given when verdict is other.

verdict_reason.description: Why the task got its verdict.

confidence.description: The writer's confidence in the result, from 0 to 1.

next_directions_suggested.description: Suggested next research directions, one per item.

proof.description: A proof write-up (on resolve_conflict and merge_person tasks, and reasoning brought in on an import_file task), which once accepted is the single authority for the status of the claims it settles.

occurrence_verdicts.description: Decisions that two or more occurrences are, or are not, the same occasion.

review.description: On a judge_review task: the review of another task (reviews are their own tasks and are never overwritten).

run_decisions.description: On a judge_review task whose payload kind is run: one keep, retract or correct decision per object the run wrote (a blanket retraction of a whole run is refused).

associates.description: On a fan_survey task: the friends, associates and neighbours studied around one person (FAN clusters live here, never as MaxGroups).

import_header_as_written.description: On an import_file task: the imported file's header, word for word (named submitters or contact details make the task living).

result.description: What the work found and decided.

step_no.description: This step's permanent number within the task, never renumbered or reused.

action.description: The kind of lookup, as a short word such as web_search or catalog_lookup.

source.description: Exactly which site, database, book or archive was searched, as written.

source_id.description: The MaxSource searched, when it is in this database.

source_url.description: The address searched, when there is one; never invented.

query.description: The exact search terms or browse path used.

span.description: The years or dates the search covered (use derivation interpreted when the span is not quoted from the source).

place.description: The place the search covered, as written.

items.description: One kind of record searched, in plain words or a MaxRecord record_type value.

record_types.description: The kinds of record the search covered.

coverage.description: What the search covered, so a later search does not repeat it blindly.

found.description: What came back, or the word nothing.

record_id.description: The record saved from this step, if any.

person_id.description: The person searched for, when the step was about one person (what step --person and dead-end --person store).

verdict_as_written.description: The outcome in the writer's own words, given when verdict is other.

confidence.description: The writer's confidence in this step's finding, from 0 to 1.

step.description: One search or lookup, recorded once and kept.

subject.description: What the proof is about: people, claims, links, unions, memberships, occurrences, records, mentions, places, groups or pairs of people.

question.description: The research question the proof answers, in plain words.

relied_on.description: Everything the proof relies on, which may never include a claim it settles (P3).

summary.description: A short summary of at most 2,000 characters, for exports.

proof_form.description: How full the write-up is; argument requires the argument field, and a proof that relies on indirect, negative, DNA or search-step evidence must be an argument (P5).

conclusion.description: What the proof concludes and what it settles.

supersedes_task_id.description: An earlier proof task that this proof replaces.

origin.description: Where the reasoning was written: in this database (maxgen), in another program (imported) or in another MAXGEN database (foreign_maxgen); only a maxgen proof can ever be accepted, count as reliable or make a claim proven.

origin_outside_ids.description: The other program's or database's ids for this reasoning.

origin_attribution.description: Who wrote the brought-in reasoning and when, word for word.

proof.description: A proof write-up: the question, what it relied on, the argument and the conclusion.

kind.description: What kind of thing this subject is (link and union both name a MaxRelationship).

id.description: The subject's id: a UUID, or record_id#mention_id for a mention.

id2.description: For a person_pair: the second person.

proof_subject.description: One thing a proof is about.

kind.description: What kind of thing the proof relies on; it names the ids that kind needs.

assertion_id.description: For a claim: its assertion id.

record_id.description: For a record, an authored record or a mention: the record.

mention_id.description: For a mention: the mention's label on that record.

dna_id.description: For a DNA match: the DNA test that holds the match.

match_id.description: For a DNA match: the match's permanent id.

task_id.description: For a search step or another proof: the task that holds it.

step_no.description: For a search step: its step number.

note.description: What this item contributes to the argument.

relied_on.description: One thing a proof relies on.

status.description: The status apply-proof copies onto that claim once the proof is accepted (proven only under rules P1 to P7).

items.description: One claim this proof settles, and how.

membership_id.description: The membership (one child's place in one parent set) to update; a membership combined into another by a merge is followed to the one it was combined into.

set_kind.description: The kind of parent set the proof settles for this membership (setting adoptive also needs the person's recorded yes, R-31; a change that would give the child two live memberships of one kind in one family is refused, R-20).

prefer.description: True records this membership as the child's preferred (main) parent set, as the prefer command would.

add_parent_link_ids.description: Parent links (parent_child records of the same child, each with a live fact) to add to this membership, such as the known mother's link when a candidate father was linked alone; the parent also fills an empty partner slot of the family.

retract.description: True retracts this membership (kept, marked retracted), such as the parent set the proof shows was wrong.

items.description: One parent-set change this proof settles.

membership_updates.description: Parent-set changes apply-proof makes after the claim statuses, under the same gates (the only way besides link that a membership's kind changes).

occurrence_ids.description: The occurrences (MaxEvent ids) judged, two or more.

verdict.description: same merges the occurrences when the task is accepted (undoably); not_same records them as distinct.

survivor_id.description: For same: the occurrence that survives the merge.

reason.description: Why they are, or are not, the same occasion.

reverted_at.description: Helper-owned: when the merge this verdict made was undone.

occurrence_verdict.description: A decision about whether two or more occurrences are one occasion.

verdict.description: The review's decision; how independent the reviewer was is worked out from the two tasks' provenance and never stored.

rejection_reason.description: Why the work was not accepted; with other, say why in notes.

notes.description: The reviewer's own words (for a decision the person made, the person's own words).

object_kind.description: What kind of object the decision is about.

id.description: The object's id in a form the retract command accepts: a UUID, or record_id#mention_id, record_id#event:ref, record_id#copy:sha256, family_id#partner:person_id, family_id#partner:absent or dna_id#match:match_id.

decision.description: What happens to the object (retracting a task sets it cancelled).

replacement_id.description: For correct: the object that replaces this one, in the same id forms.

run_decision.description: One decision of a run review about one object a run wrote.

person_id.description: The associate, when they are a person in this database.

record_id.description: The record that names the associate.

mention_id.description: The associate's mention label on that record.

mention.description: The associate as one record names them, when they are not a person in this database.

name_as_written.description: The associate's name exactly as the document gives it.

role_as_written.description: The associate's role in the document's own words.

association_type.description: The kind of tie to the person studied, in the MaxRelationship association words.

association_type_as_written.description: The kind of tie in the writer's or document's own words, given when association_type is other.

evidence.description: The one piece of evidence that shows this associate.

confidence.description: The writer's confidence in this finding, from 0 to 1.

note.description: Why this associate matters to the research.

associate.description: One friend, associate or neighbour found by a FAN survey: exactly one of person_id or mention.
